1 طَاخَ , aor. يَطِيخُ, (S, L, K,) inf. n. طَيْخٌ; (L;) as also ↓ تطيّخ ; He became charged, reproached, or upbraided, with something bad, evil, abominable, or foul, (S, L, K,) either said or done. (L.) ―
-b2- And طاخ, aor. as above, (S, L, K,) and so the inf. n., (L,) He magnified himself, or was proud. (S, L, K.) ―
-b3- And He exerted himself, or strove, and persisted, or persevered, in that which was vain. (K.) ＝
-A2- طَاخَهُ, aor. يِطِيخُهُ, (S, L, K,) inf. n. طَيْخٌ; as also طاخهُ, aor. يَطُوخُهُ, inf. n. طَوْخٌ; but the former is the more common; (TA in art. طوخ;) and ↓ طيّخهُ ; He charged, reproached, or upbraided, him with something bad, evil, abominable, or foul, (S, L, K,) either said or done. (L.) And أَصْحَابَهُ ↓ طيّخ He reviled and harassed his companions. (Aboo-Málik, TA.) ―
-b2- And طاخ الأَمْرَ, inf. n. as above, He corrupted, vitiated, or marred, the affair. (ISd, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
